title: AI researchers warn companies rushing self-improving systems despite safety risks
source_used: HuffPost via AOL (Rappler page blocked, HTTP 403)
key_facts: Researchers discuss 'recursive self-improvement' (RSI), where AI could improve itself and build its successors.
Rishub Jain, ex-Google DeepMind and founder of the nonprofit Sampura Research, fears AI improving very fast with less human oversight.
Crystal Grant of the Council on Strategic Risks worries about offensive cyber capabilities and AI agents covering their tracks.
OpenAI said in a blog post it does not yet know how to safely reach 'aligned, full RSI' and aims for an automated AI researcher by March 2028.
Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei said in September RSI efforts 'must be pursued very carefully, if at all'.
Cornell's John Thickstun says the hype outruns reality and does not expect a fully automated RSI system soon; his real concern is falling transparency and profit incentives.
quote_evidence: We do not yet know how to safely get all the way to aligned, full RSI," OpenAI said in a blog post this month
I would not predict a fully automated recursive self-improvement system anytime soon," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: Labs and researchers disagree on how close and how risky self-improving AI is.
